Abundant liquidity helped reduce overnight indexed swap rates, but the spike in oil prices heightened concerns about India's inflation trajectory and fiscal integrity.

items.story: Indian markets extended losses on Thursday, with the Sensex falling nearly 0.6% and the Nifty declining 0.17% as geopolitical tensions and elevated crude prices weighed on sentiment. Realty stocks outperformed, while IT stocks lagged. Here’s a look at the top Nifty and Sensex gainers and losers, along with the technical outlook.

items.story: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath recalled how a 15-year-old media appearance helped boost the broker’s account openings in its early days. He also revealed that he used the pseudonym “Sachin” and even faked an accent while speaking to a journalist. Kamath later turned to social media as traditional media’s influence waned.

items.story: Adhesives are essential in electronics, vehicles and other products, but they can hinder repair and recycling when bonded parts are difficult to separate cleanly. items.story: Two tiny ant fossils recovered in southern Saskatchewan are helping scientists better understand the evolutionary history of modern ants. Researchers hope continued observations will reveal why it suddenly formed and whether it could persist for decades.

Beyond expanding a century-old principle of physics, the finding could eventually lead to simpler magnetic sensors for electronics, transportation, and medical technologies.

items.headline: The universe has plenty of hydrogen. So why is star formation collapsing?
items.teaser: Star formation across the universe has fallen dramatically over the past 4.5 billion years, but astronomers have uncovered a surprising t…
items.story: Star formation across the universe has fallen dramatically over the past 4.5 billion years, but astronomers have uncovered a surprising twist: the supply of neutral hydrogen, a key ingredient for making stars, has barely declined. Using China’s FAST radio telescope and data from roughly 2.5 million galaxies observed by DESI, researchers found that star formation was about 2.5 times higher 4.5 billion years ago, while neutral hydrogen levels were only about 1.4 times higher.
